MCD.rationale: MCD presents a deteriorating fundamental picture despite its elite franchise structure. Q1 2026 showed sequential deceleration across all key metrics: revenue -7.9% QoQ, EPS -12.6% QoQ, and operating cash flow -29.6% QoQ. Cash conversion is weakening—OCF flat YoY (-0.7%) while earnings grew +6.9%, signaling quality deterioration. Net margin has compressed from 0.322 to 0.316. The balance sheet carries negative equity (-$1.29B) with $61.3B in liabilities, a structural risk in a rising-rate environment (10Y yield 4.71%, Baa yield 6.29%). The stock has declined -23% from its 365-day high of $341.75 to $262.80, trading near its floor. Macro headwinds are material: rising oil ($93.08/barrel) pressures input costs, rising rates compress valuation multiples for stable-growth franchises, and consumer sentiment is deteriorating per CEO Kempczinski's own admission. Management warned of 'meaningful deceleration' in Q2 comps, with April comps 'slightly negative' in US and International Operated Markets. The forward P/E of 20.28 vs. industry 23.01 reflects genuine caution but may not fully price in the trajectory deterioration. The Q2 earnings report on 2026-08-04 is a near-term downside catalyst given management's own warning. The franchise model's structural strengths (95% franchised, $147.9B systemwide sales, $155B brand value) are real but cannot offset the clear deterioration in earnings quality, cash conversion, and macro headwinds. The combination of weakening fundamentals, challenging macro, and a near-term earnings event with negative guidance skew warrants a strongly negative view.
